# Genprex to Highlight Dual Delivery Strategy for Diabetes Gene Therapy at Future of Cell and Gene Therapy Symposium


** November 11, 2026


[Press Releases](https://www.genprex.com/category/press-releases/)[Conferences](https://www.genprex.com/tag/conferences/)[Diabetes](https://www.genprex.com/tag/diabetes/)[gene therapy](https://www.genprex.com/tag/gene-therapy/)


*Genprex Senior Director of Quality Control & Product Development to Present Insights from Parallel AAV and Lipid-Based Development Programs*


*Presentation to Highlight Drug Development, Manufacturing and Optimization Considerations for Diabetes Gene Therapy*


AUSTIN, Texas — (Nov. 11, 2026) —[Genprex, Inc.](https://www.genprex.com/) (“Genprex” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ:[GNPX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/gnpx) ), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing gene therapies designed to restore tumor-suppressor function in cancer and insulin-producing function in diabetes,today announced that[Pier-Anne Lachance, Ph.D.](https://www.genprex.com/about/meet-our-team/) , the Company’s Senior Director of Quality Control & Product Development, will present at[Drug Discovery News’ Future of Cell and Gene Therapy Symposium](https://www.drugdiscoverynews.com/the-future-of-cell-and-gene-therapy-17023) taking place virtually Nov. 17-18, 2026.


Dr. Lachance’s presentation, titled “Building the Future of Diabetes Gene Therapy: Lessons from Parallel AAV and Lipid-Based Development Programs,” will explore Genprex’s development of two distinct gene delivery approaches for its diabetes program. The presentation will highlight scientific, manufacturing and product development considerations associated with advancing adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based and non-viral lipid-based technologies including how the approaches may inform future optimization and development strategies.


The two-day conference brings together experts from academia and industry to share advances across the cell and gene therapy pipeline. Topics include gene therapy approaches for rare and common diseases, advances in gene delivery and genome editing, process development and scalable manufacturing and the translation of cell and gene therapies to the clinic.


“Advancing gene therapies requires not only innovative science, but also a disciplined approach to delivery, manufacturing and product development,” said Ryan Confer, President and Chief Executive Officer at Genprex. “Our work evaluating both AAV-based and lipid-based approaches reflect our commitment to addressing important development challenges as we advance our diabetes gene therapy program. We are pleased to have Dr. Lachance share insights from this work with the broader cell and gene therapy community.”


Genprex is developing its diabetes gene therapy program as a potential treatment for both Type 1 diabetes (T1D) and Type 2 diabetes (T2D), with the goal of restoring the body’s insulin-producing capability. The Company’s AAV-based approach is designed to deliver the Pdx1 and MafA genes to the pancreas to reprogram pancreatic cells toward insulin-producing function. In parallel, Genprex is also evaluating a non-viral lipid-based delivery approach that could offer additional flexibility in treatment administration, including the potential for repeat dosing. Both approaches remain in preclinical development. Evaluating these delivery approaches in parallel is intended to help inform future development decisions as Genprex works to optimize its diabetes gene therapy program and advance toward IND-enabling studies.


The aforementioned presentation will be made available on Genprex’s website following the conference at[https://www.genprex.com/videos/](https://www.genprex.com/videos/) .


About Genprex, Inc.


Genprex, Inc. is a clinical-stage gene therapy company focusing on developing innovative treatments designed to restore biological functions disrupted by disease. The Company’s lead oncology program, Reqorsa® (quaratusugene ozeplasmid), a gene therapy product, is being developed for the treatment of lung cancer and is designed to deliver the TUSC2 tumor suppressor gene to help restore tumor-suppressive activity and address multiple pathways involved in cancer progression.


The Company’s lead candidate, REQORSA®, uses the systemic, non-viral ONCOPREX® Delivery System to deliver the TUSC2 tumor suppressor gene via a non-viral lipid-based nanoparticle. REQORSA is designed to restore tumor-suppressor function and is being evaluated in the Acclaim-1 and Acclaim-3 clinical trials for non-small cell lung cancer and small cell lung cancer, respectively. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Fast Track Designation to both lung cancer programs and Orphan Drug designation to the small cell lung cancer program.


Genprex is also advancing an earlier stage gene therapy program for diabetes, designed to restore insulin-producing capability through the expression of key pancreatic transcription factors. Across its programs, Genprex is focused on translating innovative gene therapy approaches into meaningful therapeutic advances for patients with significant unmet medical needs.
